lead.t: Haemorrhagic stroke – sudden neurological deficit caused by intracerebral bleeding (parenchymal haemorrhage) or subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) from rupture of a vessel.

src.t: Internal Medicine (MBIM 4100) main exam, Paper One: 3 July 2019

snip.t: Haemorrhagic stroke – sudden neurological deficit caused by intracerebral bleeding (parenchymal haemorrhage) or subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH) from rupture of a vessel.
Haemorrhagic stroke: control blood pressure, reverse anticoagulation, treat raised intracranial pressure, and refer for neurosurgery if indicated.
snip.s: Internal Medicine (MBIM 4100) main exam, Paper One: 3 July 2019

snip.t: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) – especially for haemorrhagic strokes; GCS ≤ 8 signals need for airway protection and possible neurosurgical intervention.
